by-side or in single file, we can extend the concepts discussed in Problem 2.
When multiple people are involved, the wear distribution changes:
Side-by-side movement results in a multi-peak distribution of wear, which covers the front
edge of the stairs (for upward movement) or the central part of the stairs (for downward movement).
The peaks represent the locations where each person steps, and the number of peaks indicates how
Single-file movement produces a single peak at the location of one person's step, with the
intensity of wear varying along the length of the stairs.
